reviewed_registry.note: v1 is read-only here; verdicts are recorded for the correction task and the Study 04 v2 protocol.

scope: Study 04 v1 run 20260921T1215Z-small (digest ab0f6ef5e5500775), its report, signed analysis, mechanism discussion, HANDOFF, dev-check runs and registry entries.

accepted_clauses: An unchecked read-modify-write loses 93.7% of acknowledged updates under one hot key with 16 writers (verified 3416 acknowledged, counter 215, 3201 lost).

Maintaining the portal overview with a per-row trigger costs 6.85x on whole-configuration replacement (verified w05_replace_all 573 -> 83.7 ops/s, p99 2.5 -> 42 ms), while the application rollup keeps writes near the reference.
narrowed_clauses: A lock-before-update delivers 1.76x the throughput of a version check at identical correctness: the recorded ratio is 1.76x (887 vs 503 ops/s) but the run cannot separate the lock's advantage from extra per-retry harness work, so it is an upper bound. State it as: on this one key at 16 writers in one trial, the lock delivered 1.76x, an upper bound on its advantage.
verdicts.reason: Every figure re-derived from results/20260921T1215Z-small/pg-single/*.json. The author's own discussion names the unrun -retries 1 control; the claim as written omits it.
verdicts.required_scope: one key, one installed product, 16 writers, PostgreSQL single node, small scale, one trial; not a low-contention comparison and not a read-phase number
verdicts.follow_up: Add the -retries 1 control and a writer sweep to the Study 04 v2 protocol; do not republish the 1.76x without it.

verdicts.reason: Accurate coverage gap, not a null result. Eight of eighteen designs unbuilt; no cardinality, cadence/churn, repeated randomized trials, equal-total resources, placement or YugabyteDB.
verdicts.follow_up: The gap is already owned by task-20260922T025912Z-study04-v2-protocol. This review requires that protocol to add: (a) the repeated-design instrument control (n1 first and last, >=3 trials, fresh database per cell or recorded randomized order) so the ~1.7x read floor is measured rather than assumed; (b) the -retries 1 contention control to separate lock advantage from harness charging; (c) an explicit statement that 1.76x is one point on a writer curve, not a curve. No new task is created.

review_findings: The identical-SQL read spread is real (1.59-1.66x across r01/r02/r03, n1 slowest) and the ~1.7x attribution floor must be preserved.

The proposed cause of that spread (later cell inherits a dirtier buffer cache/catalog) is not corroborated by this run's recorded order: the slowest identical-SQL cell is 8th of 10, and the last two cells beat cells 6-8 at those reads. Treat the mechanism as a hypothesis until the repeated-design control runs.
The signed analysis's '65% spread' figure is the r01 comparison (1.655x); its parenthetical example is r03 (1.593x). Presentation mismatch only; the discussion's table is precise.
Missing designs/topologies must never be read as 'would not change this'.
required_corrections: claim-10 first clause: add the upper-bound and single-key/single-trial/PostgreSQL-only scope.
Study 04 v2 protocol: add the three controls named under claim-gap-01 follow_up.
notes: No measurement was performed or authorized by this review.
Existing signed artifacts were not edited; the review adds one signed analysis and cites the others.
